action_items.task: Check if the project requirements mean the device is for TV only or also for internet-type things, and update the team.
Finish questionnaires, then spend thirty minutes on individual work thinking about discussed ideas and bringing new ones to the next meeting.

decisions.text: Teletext feature is removed from the remote.
Speech recognition feature is removed from the remote.
VCR capabilities are removed from the remote.
The remote will have a separate power button.
The location finder will use a radio signal from a separate base unit.
The location finder on the remote will output a beep.
The remote will be silver with yellow writing.
The target audience is teenagers and young professionals.

notes:
## Usability and Market Analysis
- A study of 100 people showed users dislike how remotes look, feel, and match their operating behavior.
- Users only use 10% of available buttons; the most important are channel selection, teletext, volume, and power.
- People aged 15-35 are willing to pay more for advanced features like speech recognition, while those over 35 are less likely to pay.
- The Marketing Expert noted that teenagers and young professionals are the most likely buyers.
## Feature Decisions
- Teletext is removed from the list due to internet popularity.
- Speech recognition is dropped because it is hard to program, potentially silly, and too expensive for the budget.
- VCR capabilities are dropped because VCR standards vary internationally, whereas DVD standards are consistent.
- The location finder feature is kept, using a radio signal from a separate base unit (TV or wall) that triggers a beep on the remote.
- A separate power button is required, as holding a button down is considered confusing for users.
## Design Specifications
- The remote will use a battery, button pad, pre-made chip, IR transmitter, and radio receiver.
- The location signal sender will be a separate unit sold with the remote.
- The location signal on the remote will be a buzzer/beep rather than a light.
- The remote design should include a red power button.
- The remote will be silver with yellow writing.
## Interface and Compatibility
- The team discussed a circular touch-pad interface similar to the iPod, noting its intuitive usability.
- The device uses mouse-pad technology and allows scrolling to navigate channels or volume.
- The team considered how the device might rotate and whether functions need to be switchable based on the mode (e.g., TV vs. DVD).
- They discussed the need for a function switch button to change modes between TV, DVD, and VCR.
tldr: The team reviewed usability findings and decided to target teenagers and young professionals, dropping teletext, speech recognition, and VCR features. They agreed on a silver remote with yellow writing, a separate power button, and a location finder using a radio signal and beep. The group discussed a circular touch-pad interface and assigned tasks to clarify device compatibility and prepare for the next meeting.
